title: Prefetch credit fallback protocol for multi-GPU latency smoothing
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Problem summary:

Large-model prefill/decode traffic across heterogeneous multi-GPU clusters exhibits short, high-amplitude NCCL microbursts that cause transient queue growth and kernel eviction, increasing p50/p99 latency for interactive workloads. Existing solutions (coarse batching windows, fixed token chunk sizes) either hurt tail latency or reduce throughput. We need a lightweight protocol to coordinate per-stage prefetch credits, negotiate graceful kernel fallbacks, and smooth NCCL overlap windows without a heavy global lock.

Scope and goals:
- Design and implement a prefetch credit exchange between pipeline/tensor-parallel stages that allows stages to pace prefill microbursts while preserving throughput.
- Implement a fallback kernel hint path: when credit exhaustion or NCCL contention is detected, stages should switch to a smaller- footprint attention kernel or reduced microbatch size without aborting the request.
- Add a micro-backoff and token-lease mechanism to ensure fair bandwidth sharing across concurrent requests and retry windows for stalled tokens.
- Maintain single-request determinism: output must not change semantics when falling back (only performance/latency is affected).

Proposed design (high level):
1) Credit buckets: each stage maintains a soft credit bucket representing tokens it can prefetch into KV cache. Credits replenish at a measured rate per-stage based on observed egress throughput and link bandwidth.
2) Lease tokens: a short-lived lease (10–50ms) is granted per microbatch; if the downstream stage cannot accept due to NCCL congestion, the lease can be returned or extended via a cheap rendezvous RPC.
3) Graceful fallback kernels: runtime provides two kernel profiles for attention: "fast-footprint" (lower memory, slightly lower perf) and "high-throughput" (default). The conductor can swap profiles per-microbatch when credits are low.
4) NCCL microburst smoothing: stages emit small, spread-out allreduce windows by splitting large prefill transfers into S-shaped micro-transfers using token pacing.
5) Telemetry + adaptive controller: a control loop on the conductor aggregates per-stage RTT and NCCL queue depth to adjust credit refill rates and fallback thresholds.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Minimal global coordination: prefer local per-stage heuristics and a small rendezvous endpoint for exceptional cases to avoid global slowdowns.
- Backward compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged unless the new protocol is enabled via runtime flags (configurable per-cluster).
- Memory vs latency trade: fallback kernels reduce peak memory to avoid kernel eviction, but may cost a small per-token CPU/GPU cycles; acceptance criteria will quantify acceptable regression.
- Safety: ensure no deadlock when multiple stages attempt simultaneous fallback or lease renewal—use timeouts and idempotent rendezvous.

Acceptance criteria:
- P50 latency for short interactive prefill requests (<=256 tokens) improves or remains within 5% of baseline under 80% cluster load.
- P99 latency reduces by at least 15% during high NCCL contention scenarios in internal chaos tests.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) change is within -10% to +5% compared to baseline for large batch workloads.
- No functional changes to model outputs (regression tests + golden prompts pass).
- Monitor shows reduced NCCL queue depth spikes and smoother allreduce patterns.

Testing plan and rollout:
- Unit tests for credit ledger, lease lifecycle, and kernel profile swap.
- Integration tests in the emulator with synthetic bandwidth limits and heterogeneous GPU speeds.
- Canary rollout on a small Dedicated fleet: flag-controlled rollout with telemetry hooks and automatic rollback on tail-latency regression.
- Load test matrix: 3 model sizes (7B/35B/70B), sequence lengths (512/2048), mixed concurrency levels.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Fallback churn causing oscillation between kernel profiles. Mitigation: hysteresis counters and minimum dwell time per-profile.
- Risk: Rendezvous RPC becomes a bottleneck. Mitigation: use UDP-like best-effort cache of last-known credits and limit rendezvous to edge cases.
- Risk: Subtle correctness differences with quantized kernels. Mitigation: restrict fallback kernels to numerically compatible implementations and add extensive evals.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Spike: implement a simulated credit bucket and lease workflow in the runtime emulator (owner: Liam) — 1 week.
- Telemetry: add NCCL queue depth metric and per-stage credit usage counters (owner: Asha) — 1 sprint.
- Experiment design: define chaos experiments for microburst injection and a gating dashboard (owner: SRE team) — 2 weeks.
